notes: Complex Systems 35(1) (2026) 1-9. READ IN FULL 21 September 2026 from the publisher PDF at literature/sources/knight-2026-small-collatz-rule-complex-systems-35-1.pdf. The earlier record said content.wolfram.com was egress-blocked and the paper could not be fetched; it answered 200 on 21 September. Kevin Knight, Threeven Labs, Marina del Rey, CA -- an affiliation the register did not have. DOI 10.25088/ComplexSystems.35.1.1, printed in the paper. WHAT IT IS, AND THE 30 IS NOW OBSERVED. Theorem 1: the rule K(n) simulates Collatz C(n), with THIRTY conditions modulo 30 and coefficients {375/2, 125/2, 5/3, 2/5, 3/4}, acting on numbers coded as 2^x 3^y 5^z with 2, 3, 5 as registers. Proof by showing the eight computational states occupy distinct classes mod 30. Step counts: 8m+6 to simulate an odd term 2m+1, 3m for an even term 2m. CAVEAT THE SUMMARIES OMITTED: K(n) is NOT a true generalized Collatz rule, because (3/4)n cannot be written as (a_4 n + b_4)/30; the genuine generalized form is K'(n) with SIXTY conditions. So 'thirty' is right for the rule and sixty for the generalized-Collatz object. MONKS'S 1021020 IS EXPLAINED, NOT JUST QUOTED. Knight prints Monks's Fractran rule (1/11, 136/15, 5/17, 4/5, 26/21, 7/13, 1/7, 33/4, 5/2, 7/1) and its expansion with d = lcm(11,15,17,5,21,13,7,4,2) = 1021020. This register had recorded the primorial shape 2^2*3*5*7*11*13*17 as its own arithmetic observation; the reason is that it is the lcm of the Fractran denominators. Retract the implication that the shape was unexplained. THE CYCLE SECTION, WHICH THE REGISTER DID NOT ANTICIPATE. A Collatz cycle forces (375/2)^a (125/2)^b (5/3)^c (2/5)^d (3/4)^e = 1, hence d-a-b-2e = 0, a+e-c = 0, 3a+3b+c-d = 0, solved by b = e/2 - 3a/2, c = a+e, d = 5e/2 - a/2, with a the count of odd terms, b the sum of odd terms minus that count, e half the sum of even terms. THEOREM 2: K(n) takes (5/2)m steps to simulate a C(n) cycle, m the sum of even terms; hence every K(n) cycle length is a multiple of 5 and the 3/4 branch is taken exactly 20 percent of the time. He notes p != 1 is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT (125/2 only follows 375/2). His resulting identity 2 sum_odd m_i + #odd = (1/2) sum_even m_i he calls 'a well-known property of C(n) cycles'; it is monks-2002-3x1-minus-the-plus Corollary 1 in another form, so the cycle corollary is a re-derivation by a different route. THE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, NEGATIVELY. The register asked whether this paper and the multiplicative_knight branch are the same instinct twice. They are not: this Knight removes addition by MOVING TO A THREE-REGISTER 2^x 3^y 5^z ENCODING with rational multipliers, whereas the Juggler removes it by MOVING TO THE EXPONENT and paying a floor; and the additive cocycle converted in that branch is the Bohm-Sontacchi charge of his OTHER paper, unrelated to K(n)'s registers. The trade framing this register already carried -- state space against a floor -- is confirmed by the text. WHY THE OLD DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG: Knight cites yolcu-aaronson-heule-2023-automated-collatz as reference [9] among related small devices, alongside de Mol's tag system, Korec's cellular automaton and Sterin's Wang tiles, which is how a search summary merged the two papers. Those four are named here and deliberately NOT given records; register them only if the addition-free comparison is opened as a branch. Bafina is cited as [4] for the 10^20 range: that is barina-2021-convergence-verification, now registered, and NOT the 2025 paper this register already carries.
